_comment: Subset of MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise used by the game. IDs and names follow attack.mitre.org. Descriptions are short paraphrases for teaching.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Adversaries email a malicious file (often a macro-enabled Office document) to a chosen target, relying on the user to open it.
techniques.detection: Check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results and From / Reply-To / Return-Path mismatches. Detonate attachments in a sandbox and alert on macro-enabled files from external senders.
techniques.mitigation: Block macros in files from the internet, filter attachments at the mail gateway, enforce DMARC, and train users to report suspicious mail.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Adversaries email a link that leads to a malicious download or a credential-harvesting page instead of attaching a file.
techniques.detection: Inspect URLs in mail and proxy logs for newly registered or look-alike domains and for clicks shortly after delivery.
techniques.mitigation: URL rewriting and sandboxing at the mail gateway, web filtering, and user training.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries log in with legitimate credentials they stole, blending in with normal activity instead of using malware.
techniques.detection: Baseline where and how each account normally logs on (hosts, logon types, hours) and alert on deviations, especially for service accounts.
techniques.mitigation: Least privilege, MFA, unique managed passwords for service accounts, and monitoring of privileged account use.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.description: The adversary relies on a user opening a file (for example enabling macros in a document) to run their code.
techniques.detection: Watch for Office or PDF readers spawning scripting engines, shells, or unexpected executables, and for files opened from Downloads or mail temp folders.
techniques.mitigation: Block macros from the internet, use attack surface reduction rules for Office child processes, and train users.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to run commands and scripts, often hidden and encoded, to download and launch payloads.
techniques.detection: Enable Script Block Logging (Event 4104) and module logging. Alert on -EncodedCommand, hidden windows, download cradles, and unusual parent processes.
techniques.mitigation: Constrained Language Mode, script signing, removing PowerShell v2, and limiting who can run PowerShell.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries use cmd.exe to run commands and batch scripts.
techniques.detection: Monitor cmd.exe launched by unusual parents and command lines with chained discovery or download commands.
techniques.mitigation: Application control and limiting interactive shells on servers.

techniques.name: System Services: Service Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries run a program by creating or starting a Windows service, which executes it as SYSTEM.
techniques.detection: Alert on service installs (Event 7045) with binaries in unusual paths or installed over the network from admin shares.
techniques.mitigation: Restrict who can create services remotely and require signed service binaries.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries create scheduled tasks to run their code at logon, at boot, or on a timer, often as SYSTEM, so it survives reboots.
techniques.detection: Collect Event 4698 (task created) and task XML. Look for tasks running from user-writable paths, created by non-admin users, or named to imitate vendors.
techniques.mitigation: Limit who can create tasks that run as SYSTEM, audit task creation, and remove local admin rights from regular users.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Adversaries add a Run key value or a Startup folder entry so their program launches every time the user logs on.
techniques.detection: Monitor writes to Run / RunOnce keys (Sysmon Event 13) and compare autostart entries against an approved baseline, watching for look-alike names.
techniques.mitigation: Application control, least privilege, and regular autoruns baselining.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.description: Adversaries install or modify a Windows service so their program starts automatically with high privileges.
techniques.detection: Watch Event 7045 and service registry changes for unusual binary paths and new auto-start services.
techniques.mitigation: Restrict service creation rights and monitor service configuration changes.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries encode, encrypt, or pack commands and files to hide their purpose from analysts and tools.
techniques.detection: Decode Base64 and other encodings in command lines, flag high-entropy strings, and use Script Block Logging to see de-obfuscated content.
techniques.mitigation: Antimalware with script scanning (AMSI) and behavior-based detection.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Adversaries read the memory of the LSASS process to steal password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and sometimes cleartext credentials of logged-on users.
techniques.detection: Sysmon Event 10 for processes opening lsass.exe with high access rights (such as 0x1FFFFF or 0x1010), plus dump files created by unusual processes.
techniques.mitigation: Enable LSA protection (RunAsPPL) and Credential Guard, remove local admin rights, and avoid logging privileged accounts on to workstations.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
techniques.description: Adversaries extract local account hashes from the SAM registry hive.
techniques.detection: Watch for reg.exe saving HKLM\SAM or SYSTEM hives and access to SAM files by unusual processes.
techniques.mitigation: Unique local admin passwords (LAPS) and restricting registry backup rights.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries list user and group accounts to learn who has privileges worth stealing.
techniques.detection: Alert on net user / net group / directory queries from hosts or users that do not normally run them, and on group enumeration events on domain controllers.
techniques.mitigation: Hard to prevent; focus on detection and limiting what regular users can enumerate.

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Domain Account
techniques.description: Adversaries list domain users and groups, such as Domain Admins, to find privileged accounts.
techniques.detection: Watch for net user /domain, net group "Domain Admins" /domain, and LDAP enumeration from unexpected hosts.
techniques.mitigation: Detection-focused; restrict anonymous and unnecessary directory enumeration.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries look for other hosts on the network, using ping sweeps, net view, nltest, or port probes, to plan lateral movement.
techniques.detection: Alert on ping sweeps, one host touching many internal hosts on SMB or RDP ports in a short time, and nltest /dclist from workstations.
techniques.mitigation: Network segmentation and host firewalls that block workstation-to-workstation traffic.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries gather details about the operating system and hardware of a host.
techniques.detection: Monitor systeminfo, hostname, and similar commands run by unusual parent processes.
techniques.mitigation: Detection-focused.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries use RDP with valid credentials to log on interactively to other hosts.
techniques.detection: Logon type 10 events and RDP connections (TCP 3389) between hosts that do not normally talk, especially from servers or with service accounts.
techniques.mitigation: Limit RDP to jump hosts from admin subnets, require MFA and Network Level Authentication, and deny RDP to service accounts.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries use valid credentials to reach hidden admin shares (C$, ADMIN$) over SMB to copy and run tools on remote hosts.
techniques.detection: Event 5140/5145 access to ADMIN$ or C$, logon type 3 from unusual sources, and service installs right after a network logon.
techniques.mitigation: Block SMB between workstations, use unique local admin passwords, and restrict admin share access.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
techniques.description: Adversaries use WinRM (PowerShell remoting) to run commands on remote hosts.
techniques.detection: Monitor wsmprovhost.exe child processes and WinRM connections on TCP 5985/5986.
techniques.mitigation: Restrict WinRM to admin hosts and accounts.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
techniques.description: Adversaries compress and often encrypt collected data with tools like 7-Zip or WinRAR before stealing it.
techniques.detection: Alert on archive utilities creating large archives in staging folders such as PerfLogs, Public, or Temp, especially on servers.
techniques.mitigation: Application control on servers and data loss prevention monitoring.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Adversaries hide command and control in normal-looking HTTP/HTTPS traffic, often beaconing on a regular interval.
techniques.detection: Look for regular check-ins (fixed interval with small jitter), consistent request sizes, odd user agents, and rare destination domains.
techniques.mitigation: Proxy enforcement with domain categorization, TLS inspection where allowed, and blocking newly seen domains.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
techniques.description: Adversaries tunnel command and control through DNS queries and responses, often using TXT records and long random subdomains.
techniques.detection: Watch for high volumes of TXT queries, long high-entropy subdomains under one parent domain, and hosts querying external resolvers directly.
techniques.mitigation: Force DNS through internal resolvers, block outbound port 53 from hosts, and use DNS filtering.

techniques.name: Encrypted Channel
techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt command and control traffic with a known or custom algorithm to hide its contents.
techniques.detection: Look for unusual TLS fingerprints, self-signed certificates, and encrypted traffic on non-standard ports.
techniques.mitigation: TLS inspection and egress filtering.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries download extra tools or payloads from external infrastructure into the victim network.
techniques.detection: Scripting engines or Office apps downloading executables, and new binaries written to ProgramData, Temp, or Public.
techniques.mitigation: Web filtering and blocking downloads of executables from uncategorized domains.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Adversaries steal data over the same channel they already use for command and control.
techniques.detection: Unusually large outbound transfers to C2 destinations, upload volume far above download volume, and transfers at odd hours.
techniques.mitigation: Egress filtering, data loss prevention, and blocking known C2 infrastructure.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
techniques.description: Adversaries upload stolen data to legitimate cloud storage services to blend in.
techniques.detection: Large uploads to cloud storage from servers or accounts that never use them.
techniques.mitigation: Restrict sanctioned cloud storage and inspect uploads.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt data on target systems (ransomware) to disrupt the business and extort payment.
techniques.detection: Staged encryptor binaries, ransom notes, scheduled tasks pointing at data volumes, and mass file modifications.
techniques.mitigation: Offline, tested backups; least privilege; and application control on servers.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Adversaries delete backups and shadow copies so victims cannot recover without paying.
techniques.detection: vssadmin delete shadows, wbadmin delete catalog, and backup service tampering.
techniques.mitigation: Offline backups and protecting backup infrastructure with separate credentials.
